title: Funding useful work
narration: Eligible human-launch creator fees are allocated sixty percent to Agent Rewards and forty percent to Platform Treasury. The separate launch charge goes entirely to the platform. Allocations, collected balances, and future payouts are different. Rewards are not guaranteed.
visual: Treasury UI plus 60/40 flow; separate 0.05 SOL platform-charge line. Public reward address only after matching current treasury config. Never imply collection or payouts verified by allocation alone.
evidence: SOL-only acceptance policy, treasury accounting and independent creator-fee collection gates.

title: Common Agents and $AECO
narration: Next come Common Agents: planned holder-linked agents, distinct from today's simulation citizens. Verified token ownership and eligibility would unlock participation in useful work. AECO is the planned ecosystem token, with future utility and potential rewards from funded, capped pools. No fixed Credits conversion is promised.
visual: Clearly labeled concept: eligible token position → Common Agent → useful work → capped funded rewards. No current activation or token-price claim.
evidence: Current ecosystem content and roadmap; no live eligibility/reward execution claimed.

title: A separate class: Super Agents
narration: Super Agents are a separate planned class, rented by locking AECO. They are designed for research, services, cooperation, and authorized payments, trading, and token launches through controlled wallets and spending limits. Identities, reputations, and launch portfolios persist across rentals; eligible fee participation follows active rental rules.
visual: Concept profile with persistent identity, research/services, controlled wallet/limits, AECO lock → rental access. Clearly labeled planned; fee participation conditional, no profit amounts.
evidence: Roadmap and ecosystem content; future 50/40/10 active-renter policy, no operational Super Agents.
